request.instructions:
You extract financial claims from a social media post or article so they can be checked against SEC filings.

Return only JSON, with no prose and no code fence, in this shape:
{"claims": [{"quote": "...", "claim": "...", "ticker": "...", "kind": "..."}]}

Rules for each item:
- quote: an exact contiguous span of the post, copied character for character (same language, same punctuation). Include the slide/table heading through the relevant row when its date or units are needed. For speech, use the surrounding turn or period introduction when needed. Do not combine noncontiguous excerpts.
- claim: one standalone English sentence that names the company and keeps every number, unit, period and direction word from the quote. Convert East Asian units to standard English scale words: 億 = hundred million, so 2,451 億美元 = $245.1 billion and 623 億 = $62.3 billion; 萬 = ten thousand. Write currency as $ only when the post says US dollars (美元); otherwise keep the currency it names. Do not add a period, number or company that the post does not state. If the post says "last quarter" without a date, keep "last quarter".
- ticker: the US stock ticker if the company is clear, otherwise null.
- Preserve the document's stated period in every financial claim, including growth clauses. Resolve a nearby "June quarter" from an explicit fiscal quarter/year in the release introduction. Prefer fiscal Q3 2025 to repeating a calendar end date. Period years/quarter digits may come from nearby context, but any other added number (including the day 28 in a date) MUST occur in quote: expand the exact quote to cover that heading. Never use today's date or the latest filing to fill a missing period. Do not borrow a comparison period or a different company's period. If context is ambiguous, leave the period unresolved.
- kind: "reported_fact" for results a company reported, including non-GAAP measures; "issuer_guidance" for a claim about the company's own stated guidance, expectations or financial targets; "forecast" for analysts' or other third parties' predictions; "opinion" for valuations, recommendations or judgments; "other" for anything else with a number (stock price moves, market share, user counts).
Include every sentence that contains a number about a company. Return {"claims": []} if there are none.

Post:


User-supplied document ticker context: MSFT. This is an unauthenticated issuer hint, not part of the quoted source and not financial evidence. Use it only when the document has no explicit issuer. Preserve explicitly named other issuers; never relabel their claims to match the hint. Never include this context in a quote.
Bounded extraction: return AT MOST 4 atomic claims in this window. For dense financial tables prioritize the latest explicitly labeled period and revenue, GAAP net income, diluted EPS and operating cash flow before other metrics. Preserve table units, period and GAAP/non-GAAP labels. Do not enumerate every historical cell. For a table, quote ONLY the exact row text. Read period and units from the visible headers as context, but DO NOT concatenate a header with a nonadjacent row. Do not add a title or omit intervening rows inside a quotation. A quote must still be an exact contiguous span of the original input. If a chart has no readable numeric value, do not estimate one from bar or line positions.

input.content:
Thank you, Satya, and good afternoon, everyone. Our results exceeded expectations across revenue, revenue, operating income, and earnings per share. Driven by strong demand across the Microsoft cloud. This quarter, revenue was $92.3 billion up 19% gross margin dollars increased 17% and gross margin percentage was 68% operating income increased 21% and 22% 22% in constant currency earnings per share was $4.89 and increase of 18% and 19% in constant currency when adjusted for the impact for our investment in OpenAI.

And FX was roughly in line with guidance. Operating expenses increased 6% driven by continued investments in R&D compute capacity and talent, operating margins increased slightly year over year to 50% driven by strong revenue growth platform efficiency gains and focused investments across our portfolio.

partially offset by sales mix shift to Azure. When adjusted for the impact for our investments in OpenAI
